review_notes: I read the whole file and checked how its simp lemmas are used elsewhere in lean/OAI. The pieces I checked were the nestedX/nestedY coordinate simp lemmas, the nestedEvalHom_C/X lemmas, and the call sites of eval_nestedX and eval_nestedY (DivisibleInflection, PolynomialLocalGraph, RealCriticalPoints). The coordinate simp lemmas (nestedX_C, nestedX_X_zero/one, nestedY_C, nestedY_X_zero/one) and the nestedEvalHom_C/X lemmas look sound. They have distinct left-hand sides, and each rewrites a coordinate expression to a smaller normal form. I did not find any cycle or competing rules. The one gap is that the two bridge lemmas are not tagged simp. I could not run Lean, so I did not test whether adding the attribute interacts with the existing `Matrix.cons_val` simp lemmas. The suggestion is hedged for that reason.

findings.excerpt: nestedEvalHom R x y (nestedY R Q) = MvPolynomial.eval ![x,y] Q
findings.problem: The file builds a simp interface for nestedX, nestedY and nestedEvalHom. It tags the constants, the variables and the evaluation of `C` and `X`. The two lemmas that connect these pieces are plain theorems. They rewrite `nestedEvalHom _ _ _ (nestedY _ Q)` and `nestedEvalHom _ _ _ (nestedX _ Q)` to the canonical `MvPolynomial.eval ![x,y] Q`. The left-hand side is strictly more complex, so the rewrite terminates. Because the lemmas are not simp, callers rebuild the rewrite by hand. `PolynomialLocalGraph.verticalPolynomial_eval` uses `have h := eval_nestedY ℝ Q x y` followed by `change ... at h` and `simpa only`. `RealCriticalPoints` restates the lemma to feed it to `beval`. `DivisibleInflection.eval_swap` does `have h1 := eval_nestedX ...; rw [nestedX_swap] at h1; exact h1.symm.trans (eval_nestedY ...)`. In each case simp cannot fire on `nestedEvalHom R x y (nestedY R Q)`. The argument order of `eval_nestedX` is also swapped: it is stated with `nestedEvalHom R y x` on the left and `![x,y]` on the right. That order suits a simp lemma, but it is confusing as a manual rewrite.
findings.proposed_change: Add `@[simp]` to `eval_nestedY` and `eval_nestedX`. The left-hand sides are the head pattern `nestedEvalHom R _ _ (nestedY R _)` / `(nestedX R _)`, and the right-hand side is `MvPolynomial.eval ![x,y] Q`, which contains no `nestedEvalHom`. Then `verticalPolynomial_eval` and `eval_swap` can be closed by `simp`/`simpa` without the `have`/`change`/`trans` plumbing. Check that the new rules do not clash with the simp-normal form of `![x,y]`. If they do, state a variant with `Matrix.cons_val`-normalized arguments instead.
findings.benefit: Evaluating a nested polynomial built from `nestedX` or `nestedY` would reduce to the one multivariate `MvPolynomial.eval` form by plain `simp`. Downstream proofs would no longer re-derive this bridge by hand, and the simp set in the file would cover the evaluation interface it already starts to expose.
